label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: The shopper said it reached payment, but no payment form was found.

findings.problem: Focus moved onto unnamed div elements after using the skip link, so I could not tell where I was; one extra Tab was needed before reaching a real link.
Reaching any product by keyboard needs a long walk through the header and category links; the skip link only lands on an unnamed div.
Activating a category link gave no visible change at first; the page content stayed the same until I read again, so I was unsure whether the click worked.

About 25 Tab presses were needed to get from the top to the first product: 11 sub-category links, carousel buttons, 7 filter buttons and Sort By come first, and the skip link does not jump to the product grid.

Each product card has a wishlist button and a Buy it now button as separate stops; the Buy it now button name includes the price, which is clear. I never perceived a payment form, the tool only reported that the payment step was reached after I pressed Buy it now, so I cannot confirm cart, shipping or payment pages.
